spec_provided_observability.name: Header ACK / NACK
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Per-frame success indicator on SDA 9th SCL bit during address header.

spec_provided_observability.name: T-Bit Parity (Write)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Per-byte data integrity check on Master-write words; mismatch = error type S2.

spec_provided_observability.name: T-Bit End-of-Data (Read)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Slave-driven flow-control on read; 0 = end, 1 = continue. Master may force end via Sr.

spec_provided_observability.name: IBI Address Arbitration
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Slave-initiated request visibility: Open-Drain SDA arbitration on Slave Dynamic Address (RnW=1) starting from Bus Available Condition.

spec_provided_observability.name: Hot-Join Address (7'h02)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Detection of joining devices; mappable to a controller interrupt.

spec_provided_observability.name: Bus Conditions
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Bus Free (≥ tCAS), Bus Available (≥ tAVAL), Bus Idle (≥ tIDLE) — observable timing windows.

spec_provided_observability.name: HDR Exit Pattern
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Detected by every device; signals return to SDR mode after any HDR session.

spec_provided_observability.name: BCR / DCR / PID
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Read-only protocol-level capability registers, exposed through GETBCR / GETDCR / GETPID Direct CCCs.

spec_provided_observability.name: GETSTATUS CCC (0x90)
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Per-slave operating status: MSb-first 2-byte response per Tables 40-41 — includes pending interrupt, protocol error, activity state.

spec_provided_observability.name: SDR Error Types S0..S6
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Slave-side error taxonomy: S0 illegal address, S1 CCC parity, S2 write parity, S3 read parity, S4 monitor error, S5 NACKed IBI, S6 optional self-test.

spec_provided_observability.name: SDR Error Types M0..M2
spec_provided_observability.purpose: Master-side error taxonomy: M0 unexpected NACK, M1 invalid CCC return, M2 bus error / recovery escalation.

interrupt_sources.trigger: Slave drove its Dynamic Address (RnW=1) starting from Bus Available Condition.
Slave drove Hot-Join Address 7'h02 (RnW=0) starting from Bus Idle Condition.
Secondary Master drove its Dynamic Address (RnW=0) in arbitrable header.
T-Bit parity violation on Master-write byte (S2 / M0).
Slave drove T=0 on read data.
HDR Exit Pattern observed on the bus.

interrupt_request: I3C is unique in that the protocol itself carries In-Band Interrupts (IBI) over SDA — no separate IRQ pin is required. Concrete controllers also expose conventional MCU interrupts for the controller events listed above.
notes: MIPI I3C Basic v1.0 is a wire-level specification; DFT / scan / BIST / JTAG architecture lives at the SoC integration level. The above lists protocol-level observable conditions any compliant controller should expose. Annex C of the spec contains the normative FSMs for Main Master, Slave Interrupt Request, DAA, Hot-Join, Secondary Master Request, and Master Regaining Bus Ownership.
